14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278:

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324:

326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```

336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead

341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown

348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]

353: \```
354: 
355: **AFTER**: [Solution description]

359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale

371: 
372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
373: 
374: **Format**:

381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |

384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison

388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions

394: \```markdown

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

21: 
22: ### Location & Naming

25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only

38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.

73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95:

98: ```markdown

100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!

105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes

109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!

193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

245: - Root cause analysis required

253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed

262: - Quick reference

264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`

332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```

337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006:

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

15: # Org Chart / Responsibility Map
16: 
17: ## 1. OVERVIEW
18: 
19: **Best for:** human teams, agent teams, support escalation maps, role ownership, routing maps, and any hierarchy where the reader needs to know *who owns what* rather than just parent → child structure.
20: 
21: Use **Org Chart** instead of **Tree** when the nodes are people, agents, teams, roles, or accountable owners. A tree shows generic hierarchy. An org chart shows responsibility, invocation paths, and coverage gaps.
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
26: - Root owner or front door at top center. Use one coral focal node for the person/team/agent that receives ambiguous work.
27: - Tier 1 nodes are departments, pods, queues, or primary routing buckets. Keep them horizontally aligned.
28: - Tier 2 nodes are responsible owners or specialists. If there are more than 8 specialists, group them under pod nodes instead of making one giant row.
29: - Use orthogonal connectors: vertical drop from parent → horizontal bus → vertical drops to children. No diagonal lines.
30: - Each node should answer three questions when space allows:
31:   1. **Name** — human-readable role/person/agent in Geist sans.
32:   2. **How to invoke** — Slack handle, queue, issue prefix, or trigger in Geist Mono.
33:   3. **Scope** — 2–4 terse ownership words, not a paragraph.
34: - Show non-Slack / not-yet-live owners with dashed optional styling rather than hiding them. Missing routes are operationally important.
35: - Put escalation / approval rules in a small side callout or footer strip, not as extra org nodes.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 3. NODE TREATMENTS
40: - **Front door / command center:** focal treatment (`accent-tint` + `accent`).
41: - **Team / pod / department:** backend treatment (white + `ink`).
42: - **Individual agent / owner:** store or external treatment depending on whether it is active in the system.
43: - **Gap / needs setup:** optional dashed treatment.
44: - **Approval gate:** security treatment, separate from reporting hierarchy.
45: 
46: ---
47: 
48: ## 4. COMPLEXITY BUDGET
49: - Max visible org nodes: 12. If more, create an overview org chart plus separate detail charts per pod.
50: - Max depth: 4 tiers.
51: - Max direct reports under one parent: 5. If there are more, introduce grouping nodes.
52: - Max coral nodes: 1. The org chart's job is clarity, not highlighting everything.
53: - Max side callouts: 2.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 5. ANTI-PATTERNS
58: - Using a swimlane when the user's real question is "who does what?" Swimlanes explain process; org charts explain ownership.
59: - Drawing every person/agent as an identical box. It hides the front door, specialists, gaps, and escalation paths.
60: - Cramming full job descriptions into nodes. Keep scope phrases short and move detail to summary cards below.
61: - Showing unavailable / not-yet-wired agents as normal active owners. Use dashed optional styling so gaps are visible.
62: - Repeating Slack handles in body paragraphs when a node sublabel can carry the invocation path.
63: - Floating legends in the org area. Use the standard bottom legend strip.
64: 
65: ---
66: 
67: ## 6. EXAMPLES
68: - `assets/diagrams/org-chart.html` — minimal light
69: - `assets/diagrams/org-chart-dark.html` — minimal dark
70: - `assets/diagrams/org-chart-full.html` — full editorial

14: 
15: # Process
16: 
17: ## 1. OVERVIEW
18: 
19: **Best for:** sequential business processes with multiple actors/divisions where the reader needs to see *who* does *what*, *what data* enters and leaves each step, and *which tools* are used — not just the step order. Covers responsibility audits, data-quality gate reviews, cross-divisional handoff maps, and end-to-end workflow documentation.
20: 
21: Prefer swimlane (simpler) when the data types and tools don't matter. Prefer process when each step's input/output payload and responsible team must be legible at a glance.
22: 
23: This type is **parametric** — the inputs schema in §2 drives every coordinate via the formulas in §3. Two generations from the same inputs must produce visually identical SVG. The rule shapes mirror `type-data-flow.md` so color override, IN/OUT chip semantic, and reproducibility checklist read identically across types.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. INPUTS — THE PARAMETER CONTRACT
28: 
29: ```yaml
30: lanes:                              # 1..6 horizontal swimlanes (top to bottom)
31:   - { name: ["RD&E"],                 key: "RDE" }
32:   - { name: ["IT"],                   key: "IT"  }
33:   - { name: ["FIELD", "SERVICES"],    key: "FLD" }
34:   - { name: ["SURVEY", "SERVICES"],   key: "SVY" }
35:   - { name: ["HOUSEHOLD", "UNIT"],    key: "HHU" }
36:   - { name: ["COMMS &", "MARKETING"], key: "CMM" }
37: 
38: steps:                              # 1..12 vertical step columns (left to right)
39:   - { number: "1",  label: "Design"   }
40:   - { number: "2",  label: "Build"    }
41:   - { number: "3",  label: "Test", focal: true }       # focal step header chip — accent fill
42:   - { number: "4",  label: "Train"    }
43:   # ... up to 12
44: 
45: nodes:                              # explicit per-cell entries; empty cells render nothing
46:   - { lane: "RDE", step: 0,  title: "Survey design",      sub: "questionnaire · sampling", tool: "Excel · CSPro",
47:       chips: {in: null,  out: "FL"} }              # first step has no input chip
48:   - { lane: "IT",  step: 1,  title: "Build app",          sub: "form + validation",        tool: "CSPro · scripts",
49:       chips: {in: "FL", out: "TB"}, color: "#5a7d9a" }    # slate-blue — data quality concern
50:   - { lane: "RDE", step: 2,  title: "Pilot test",         sub: "field debug",              tool: "tablet · script",
51:       chips: {in: "TB", out: "TB"}, focal: true }   # focal node — accent border
52:   - { lane: "FLD", step: 3,  title: "Train enumerators",  sub: "protocols · safety",       tool: "manual",
53:       chips: {in: "TB", out: "LS"}, color: "#b85450" }    # rust-red — governance / training
54:   # ... etc
55: 
56: arrows:                             # explicit edges; styles bind to topology (see §4)
57:   - { from: {lane: "RDE", step: 0}, to: {lane: "IT",  step: 1}, style: "normal" }
58:   - { from: {lane: "IT",  step: 1}, to: {lane: "RDE", step: 2}, style: "focal-in" }     # accent — into focal
59:   - { from: {lane: "RDE", step: 2}, to: {lane: "FLD", step: 3}, style: "focal-out" }    # accent — out of focal
60:   - { from: {lane: "RDE", step: 2}, to: {lane: "IT",  step: 1}, style: "trigger" }      # dashed trigger
61:   # ... etc
62: 
63: dark: false
64: ```
65: 
66: **Reserved field semantics:**
67: - `lanes[k].key` — the 3-letter role badge text shown inside every node in that lane.
68: - `lanes[k].name` — 1 or 2 line lane label; uppercase mono.
69: - `steps[j].focal: true` — exactly **one** step may declare this. Header chip renders in accent.
70: - `nodes[i].focal: true` — exactly **one** node may declare this. Renders with accent border (§6).
71: - `nodes[i].chips` — `{in: "<CODE>", out: "<CODE>"}` object (either side `null` to omit). Codes from §9. **Skip** the input chip on the first step's nodes, **skip** the output chip on the last step's nodes (no upstream / downstream).
72: - `nodes[i].color` — optional **per-node color override**. Any valid `"#hex"` string; the §5 palette is recommended for cross-diagram consistency.
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 3. LAYOUT FORMULAS — DETERMINISTIC GEOMETRY
77: 
78: ```
79: label_col_w      = 140
80: step_slot_w      = 112                                # 100-px node + 12-px corridor
81: right_pad        = 28
82: n_steps          = len(steps)
83: n_lanes          = len(lanes)
84: 
85: # Canvas
86: viewBox_w        = label_col_w + n_steps * step_slot_w + right_pad   # 11 steps → 1400
87: header_h         = 36
88: lane_h           = 80
89: has_color_row    = any(node.color or step.color or lane.color in inputs)
90: legend_h         = 100 if has_color_row else 80       # 4 rows when colors are present
91: viewBox_h        = header_h + n_lanes * lane_h + legend_h            # 6 lanes, no colors → 596; with → 616
92: 
93: # Header strip (top)
94: chip_y           = 8
95: chip_w           = 16                                  # 20 if step.number has 2 digits
96: chip_h           = 16
97: chip_rx          = 8                                   # pill
98: 
99: # Lane positions
100: lane_y_top(k)    = header_h + k * lane_h               # 36, 116, 196, 276, 356, 436
101: lane_y_mid(k)    = lane_y_top(k) + lane_h/2            # 76, 156, 236, 316, 396, 476
102: lane_label_x     = label_col_w / 2                     # 70
103: 
104: # Step / node centers
105: step_cx(j)       = label_col_w + 8 + j * step_slot_w + node_w/2      # 198, 310, 422, ...
106:                                                                       # (8-px gutter inside content area)
107: 
108: # Nodes
109: node_w           = 100
110: node_h           = 64
111: node_x(j)        = step_cx(j) - node_w/2
112: node_y(k)        = lane_y_top(k) + (lane_h - node_h)/2     # 8-px top/bottom margin inside lane
113: 
114: # Legend strip (bottom)
115: legend_y_top     = header_h + n_lanes * lane_h
116: legend_row_y     = [legend_y_top + 16, legend_y_top + 37,
117:                     legend_y_top + 58, legend_y_top + 79]
118: ```
119: 
120: ### 3.1 Background structure
121: 
122: - Paper fill across full viewBox.
123: - Dot pattern: 22×22 grid, `circle r=0.8`, `fill rgba(45,49,66,0.10)`. Opacity 0.55.
124: - Alternating lane tints: odd-indexed lanes (0, 2, …) receive `rgba(45,49,66,0.018)` fill from `x=140` to `viewBox_w`.
125: - Lane dividers: horizontal hairlines at every `lane_y_top(k)` and at `legend_y_top`; stroke `rgba(45,49,66,0.12)` width 0.8.
126: - Label column right border: vertical hairline at `x = label_col_w`, stroke `rgba(45,49,66,0.20)` width 1, from `y = header_h` to `y = legend_y_top`.
127: 
128: ### 3.2 Step header chip + label
129: 
130: Per step `j`:
131: 
132: ```
133: chip_w(j)        = 20 if len(step.number) >= 2 else 16
134: chip_x(j)        = step_cx(j) - chip_w(j)/2
135: number_anchor    = (step_cx(j), chip_y + 11)
136: label_anchor     = (step_cx(j), 32)              # 8-px gap below chip
137: ```
138: 
139: **Chip** (the numbered pill at the top of each column):
140: - Default fill: `rgba(45,49,66,0.12)`, number text ink.
141: - Focal fill: `rgba(235,108,54,0.20)`, number text accent (§6).
142: - Per-step `color` override (§5): replaces the fill with `rgba(C, 0.20)` and the number fill with `C`.
143: 
144: **Label** (the uppercase mono text below the chip):
145: - Renders `steps[j].label` (uppercased), anchored at `label_anchor`.
146: - Font: Geist Mono 6 px, weight 500, `letter-spacing="0.12em"`, `text-anchor="middle"`.
147: - Default fill: muted (`#4f5d75` light / `#bfc0c0` dark).
148: - Focal fill: accent (`#eb6c36` light / `#f08a59` dark).
149: - Per-step `color` override: fill = `C` (matches the chip number color).
150: - Keep labels short (≤ 9 chars). Long labels truncate; if you need more, abbreviate.
151: 
152: ### 3.3 Lane labels
153: 
154: One or two-line mono label, all uppercase, letter-spacing 0.08em, font-size 8, fill muted. Centered at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k))`:
155: - Single-line: anchored at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) + 4)`
156: - Two-line: lines at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) - 4)` and `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) + 4)`
157: 
158: Per-lane `color` override (§5): replaces the label fill with `C` and the lane stripe tint with `rgba(C, 0.04)`.
159: 
160: ### 3.4 Node content layout (inside the 100×64 rect)
161: 
162: ```
163: role_chip          rect 14×10 at (node_x+4, node_y+4),  rx=2
164: role_chip_text     centered at (node_x+11, node_y+12), font-size=6, weight=600
165:                                                                 # text = lanes[k].key (3-letter lane code)
166: title              centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+26),  font-size=9 sans semibold
167: in→out             centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+40),  font-size=6.5 mono muted
168: tool               centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+52),  font-size=6.5 mono soft
169: data chip IN       rect 16×8 at (node_x+4,   node_y+54), rx=2      # payload entering
170: data chip OUT      rect 16×8 at (node_x+80,  node_y+54), rx=2      # payload leaving
171: ```
172: 
173: **Role chip text rule:** the badge inside each node renders `lanes[k].key` where `k` is the node's lane index — **not** the step number (the step number already lives in the column header chip at the top, §3.2). Showing the lane key as the node badge gives each node a self-contained "who" identifier that survives when a single node is excerpted out of context. Mirrors the same rule in `type-data-flow.md` §3.4.
174: 
175: Empty cells (no node entry) render **nothing**. No placeholder rect, no role chip, no label.
176: 
177: **Chip-vs-tool-text collision rule:** chips sit at `node_y + 54..62`; tool text baseline is at `node_y + 52`. If a node has a two-line title (rare), increase node_h to 72 OR omit the chips for that node. Default behaviour: omit chips on collision.
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 4. CONNECTOR RULES (MANDATORY)
182: 
183: Three styles, bound to topology. Connectors drawn **before** all node rects (z-order rule).
184: 
185: | `style` | Stroke | Width | Dash | Marker | When required |
186: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
187: | `normal` | `#4f5d75` (muted) | 1.0 | — | `arrow` | Standard data hand-off between steps or actors. Unlabelled. |
188: | `focal-in` / `focal-out` | `#eb6c36` (accent) | 1.2 | — | `arrow-accent` | Every edge whose endpoint is the focal node (`focal-in`) or origin is the focal node (`focal-out`). |
189: | `trigger` | `#4f5d75` (muted) | 1.0 | `4,3` | `arrow-sm` | Orchestration trigger (scheduler → tool, manual override → upstream step). Unlabelled. |
190: 
191: **Defs block** (required, three markers):
192: 
193: ```svg
194: <defs>
195:   <pattern id="dots" width="22" height="22" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
196:     <circle cx="11" cy="11" r="0.8" fill="rgba(45,49,66,0.10)"/>
197:   </pattern>
198:   <marker id="arrow"        markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="#4f5d75"/></marker>
199:   <marker id="arrow-accent" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="#eb6c36"/></marker>
200:   <marker id="arrow-sm"     markerWidth="6" markerHeight="5" refX="5" refY="2.5" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 6 2.5, 0 5" fill="#4f5d75"/></marker>
201: </defs>
202: ```
203: 
204: ### 4.1 Routing rules (non-negotiable)
205: 
206: **Single-bend right-angle:** exit RIGHT → corridor → enter TOP (↓ destination below) or BOTTOM (↑ destination above).
207: 
208: - Source-side: exit at `(node_x + 100, lane_y_mid(src_lane))` — node's right edge, vertical center.
209: - Destination-side: enter at `(step_cx(dst_step), node_y(dst_lane))` for downward, or `(step_cx(dst_step), node_y(dst_lane) + 64)` for upward.
210: - Corner radius: 8-px Q-bezier at the bend.
211: - Same-lane edges (rare — same lane, adjacent steps): horizontal `<line>` from src right to dst left.
212: - **No diagonals.** **No left-side entry.** **No exit from the top/bottom of a node.**
213: 
214: ```svg
215: <!-- Downward (destination lane > source lane) -->
216: <path d="M {rx},{src_cy} H {dst_cx - 8} Q {dst_cx},{src_cy} {dst_cx},{src_cy + 8} V {dst_top}"
217:       fill="none" stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
218: 
219: <!-- Upward (destination lane < source lane) -->
220: <path d="M {rx},{src_cy} H {dst_cx - 8} Q {dst_cx},{src_cy} {dst_cx},{src_cy - 8} V {dst_bottom}"
221:       fill="none" stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
222: 
223: <!-- Same lane (adjacent step) -->
224: <line x1="{src_right}" y1="{lane_cy}" x2="{dst_left}" y2="{lane_cy}"
225:       stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
226: ```
227: 
228: - **Z-order:** all `<path>` and `<line>` connectors emitted **before** any node `<rect>`.
229: - **Markers:** exactly one `marker-end` per path. Never `marker-start`.
230: - **Labels:** all process arrows are unlabelled by default. The step number + the actor lane carry the semantic; a label on every arrow is noise. Only label an arrow if it represents a non-step concept (re-test loop, escalation) — then use a paper-masked rect behind 6.5-px mono text.
231: 
232: ### 4.2 Crossings
233: 
234: Avoid. The corridor x position (8 px before destination node) is the only routing column — if two arrows would cross there, **swap step assignments** or **split into two diagrams** rather than introducing a bend-around. Crossings hide the underlying control flow.
235: 
236: ---
237: 
238: ## 5. COMPONENT COLOR OVERRIDE
239: 
240: Any node, lane, or step accepts an optional `color: "#hex"`. Mirrors `type-data-flow.md` §5 and `type-high-level.md` §4.4 so the rule reads identically across types.
241: 
242: ### 5.1 Per-node `color`
243: 
244: Applied to:
245: 
246: | Element | Light | Dark |
247: |---|---|---|
248: | Container fill (`rect`) | `rgba(C, 0.06)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.10)` |
249: | Container stroke | `rgba(C, 0.35)` (stroke-width 1) | `rgba(C_light, 0.45)` |
250: | Role chip fill | `rgba(C, 0.18)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.22)` |
251: | Role chip text | `C` | `C_light` |
252: | Title text | `C` | `C_light` |
253: | Sub-label (in → out) | **unchanged** (muted) | **unchanged** (muted) |
254: | Tool label | **unchanged** (soft) | **unchanged** (soft) |
255: | Data-type chips | **unchanged** | **unchanged** |
256: | Arrows touching this node | **unchanged** — topology-driven | **unchanged** |
257: 
258: `C_light` = the same hex lightened ~15% for dark-mode contrast (e.g., `#b85450` → `#d97a78`).
259: 
260: ### 5.2 Per-step `color`
261: 
262: Replaces the step header chip's fill with `rgba(C, 0.20)` and the chip's number text fill with `C`. The legend's matching step entry uses the same colors.
263: 
264: ### 5.3 Per-lane `color`
265: 
266: Replaces the lane stripe tint with `rgba(C, 0.04)` and the lane label text fill with `C`. Use sparingly — lane tints are easy to over-apply.
267: 
268: ### 5.4 Rules
269: 
270: - **Never on focal nodes / focal steps.** The accent already carries that signal. A `color` on a focal element is ignored.
271: - **Never on arrows.** Arrows are topology-driven. If you want a colored edge, pick a different `style` from §4, not a color override.
272: - **Cap at 3 custom-colored elements** per diagram (nodes + lanes + steps combined), in addition to the focal pair (focal node + focal step header). Above 3 the visual signal starts to fragment.
273: - **Subtitle and tool labels stay muted** regardless of any component `color`.
274: 
275: ### 5.5 Semantic palette (recommended)
276: 
277: Same palette as `type-high-level.md`, `type-dp-integration.md`, `type-data-flow.md`:
278: 
279: - `#b85450` rust-red — Security / Identity / Governance (access control, training, approvals)
280: - `#5a7d9a` slate-blue — Observability / Quality (data quality gates, validation, monitoring)
281: - `#7a8c47` olive-green — Data Products / Publication (consumer-ready outputs, releases)
282: - `#8c6d3f` warm-brown — Backup / DR / Archive
283: 
284: ---
285: 
286: ## 6. FOCAL RULE
287: 
288: The process diagram has three focal slots, exactly one entry each:
289: 
290: - **One focal step** (`steps[j].focal: true`) — typically the analytical or decision pivot (Test, Approve, Validate). Header chip and legend chip render in accent.
291: - **One focal node** (`nodes[i].focal: true`) — the node that *receives* the critical handoff. Accent border + accent role chip + ink title (title text stays ink so it's still readable; only the border + role chip carry the accent).
292: - **One focal arrow set** (`style: focal-in` and `focal-out`) — edges into and out of the focal node. Accent solid strokes.
293: 
294: If zero or >1 of any focal slot are declared, halt and ask the user.
295: 
296: ---
297: 
298: ## 7. DARK MODE
299: 
300: | Token | Light | Dark |
301: |---|---|---|
302: | Paper | `#f5f5f5` | `#2d3142` |
303: | Ink | `#2d3142` | `#f5f5f5` |
304: | Muted | `#4f5d75` | `#bfc0c0` |
305: | Soft | `#7a8399` | `#8e98ac` |
306: | Accent | `#eb6c36` | `#f08a59` |
307: | Dot pattern | `rgba(45,49,66,0.10)` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.10)` |
308: | Lane tint | `rgba(45,49,66,0.018)` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.025)` |
309: | Dividers | `rgba(45,49,66,0.12)` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.12)` |
310: | Label col divider | `rgba(45,49,66,0.20)` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.22)` |

312: | Focal chip fill | `rgba(235,108,54,0.20)` | `rgba(240,138,89,0.22)` |

314: | Default node stroke | `rgba(45,49,66,0.25)` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.20)` |
315: | Focal node fill | `rgba(235,108,54,0.08)` | `rgba(240,138,89,0.12)` |
316: | Focal node stroke | `#eb6c36` | `#f08a59` |
317: | Custom component colors | `C` | `C_light` (lighten ~15%) |

319: ---
320: 
321: ## 8. REPRODUCIBILITY CHECKLIST (TASTE GATE)
322: 
323: Before emitting SVG, verify **every** item:
324: 
325: 1. `viewBox = "0 0 {viewBox_w} {viewBox_h}"` derived via §3.
326: 2. Header strip at `y=0..36`; legend strip at `y=legend_y_top..viewBox_h` (`legend_y_top = 36 + n_lanes * 80`).
327: 3. Every node at `(step_cx(j) - 50, lane_y_top(k) + 8)` size `100×64`.
328: 4. Empty cells render nothing — no placeholder rect, no text.
329: 5. Exactly **one** focal step (`steps[j].focal: true`).
330: 6. Exactly **one** focal node (`nodes[i].focal: true`).
331: 7. Focal-touching arrows use `style: focal-in` / `focal-out` (accent).
332: 8. All other arrows `style: normal` (muted solid) or `style: trigger` (muted dashed). Unlabelled by default.
333: 9. All arrows emitted before any node rect (z-order rule).
334: 10. Single-bend right-angle routing only — exit right, enter top/bottom. No diagonals. Q-bezier `r=8` at each bend.
335: 11. Custom component colors ≤ 3 (in addition to the focal pair). Arrows never recolored by component `color`.
336: 12. Subtitle and tool labels stay muted regardless of any component `color`. Input chip skipped on first step's nodes, output chip skipped on last step's nodes.
337: 
338: ---
339: 
340: ## 9. DATA-TYPE CHIPS REFERENCE (INPUT + OUTPUT)
341: 
342: Same catalog as `type-data-flow.md` §9.
343: 
344: - **Input chip** at `(node_x+4, node_y+54)` — bottom-**left**. Payload entering the node.
345: - **Output chip** at `(node_x+80, node_y+54)` — bottom-**right**. Payload leaving the node.
346: - Either chip may be omitted (first/last step, unknown payload).
347: 
348: ### Chip codes
349: 
350: | Code | Color (light) | Color (dark) | Meaning |
351: |------|---------------|--------------|---------|
352: | `LS` | `#7c8f6f` sage | `#9caf8f` | List / assignment / task |
353: | `DB` | `#5c7899` dusty-blue | `#82a0c0` | Dataset / tabular records |
354: | `TB` | `#b8915a` mustard | `#d3ad7a` | Table (analysis-ready) |
355: | `FL` | `#9c6b50` rust-brown | `#b88670` | File / document / report |
356: | `WB` | `#6e6479` slate | `#8d8298` | Web / press / public release |
357: | N/A | omit chip entirely | — | Unknown or not applicable |
358: 
359: Text inside chip: white, font-size 5, weight 700, mono.
360: 
361: Data-type chip colors are a **separate semantic axis** from the per-node color override (§5). Chip colors describe *payload format*; node color describes *concern type*. A node can have both an `out: TB` mustard chip and a rust-red border simultaneously.
362: 
363: ---
364: 
365: ## 10. LEGEND (3- OR 4-ROW STRIP)
366: 
367: Each row introduced by a category label at `x = label_col_w + 4` (= 144). The default legend has **3 rows** (`STEPS` / `DATA TYPE` / `FLOW`); when one or more nodes carry a `color` override (§5), add a 4th `CONCERN` row and grow `legend_h` to 100.
368: 
369: - **Row 1 — `STEPS`** at `y = legend_y_top + 16`: repeat the header chips with their labels. Focal step keeps accent fill.
370: - **Row 2 — `DATA TYPE`** at `y = legend_y_top + 37`: one swatch per chip type actually used in the diagram. Append a small sub-hint in muted mono: `left chip = input · right chip = output`.
371: - **Row 3 — `CONCERN`** (only when color overrides are present) at `y = legend_y_top + 58`: one mini-rect per custom color used, with its semantic label.
372: - **Row 4 — `FLOW`** (position depends on whether `CONCERN` row exists): one segment per arrow style actually used, with marker + label.
373: 
374: ---
375: 
376: ## 11. COMPLEXITY BUDGET
377: 
378: | Dimension | Max |
379: |---|---|
380: | Lanes (actors) | 6 |
381: | Steps | 12 |
382: | Nodes per lane | Nodes = active steps only — empty cells are invisible |
383: | Labelled arrows | 0 by default (label only for non-step concepts) |
384: | Data-type chips per node | 2 (input + output) |
385: | Custom-colored elements (§5) | 3 (in addition to focal node + focal step) |
386: 
387: Above 6 lanes or 12 steps: split into two diagrams (overview + detail).
388: 
389: ---
390: 
391: ## 12. ANTI-PATTERNS
392: 
393: - **Placeholder empty cells** — if an actor doesn't participate in a step, leave the cell empty (no box, no text).
394: - **Diagonal arrows** — every connector must have exactly one right-angle bend. No direct straight lines between nodes in different lanes.
395: - **Left/right port entry on a vertical-dominant arrow** — always exit right, enter top or bottom.
396: - **More than one focal step / focal node** — pick the single most critical operation.
397: - **Unlabelled lanes** — every swimlane must identify its actor.
398: - **All arrows the same style** — orchestration triggers must be dashed to distinguish them from data-flow connectors.
399: - **`color` override on a focal element** — ignored. Accent always wins.
400: - **Custom-colored arrows** — connectors are topology-driven; `color` on a node never spreads to its edges.
401: - **Lane tints over-applied** — a tint on every lane reads as decoration, not signal. Apply to ≤1 lane.
402: - **Data-type chips in a double-line-name node** — skip the chips or shorten the name to one line.
403: - **More than 12 steps without splitting** — use an overview + detail pair.
404:
