14: 
15: # Process
16: 
17: ## 1. OVERVIEW
18: 
19: **Best for:** sequential business processes with multiple actors/divisions where the reader needs to see *who* does *what*, *what data* enters and leaves each step, and *which tools* are used — not just the step order. Covers responsibility audits, data-quality gate reviews, cross-divisional handoff maps, and end-to-end workflow documentation.
20: 
21: Prefer swimlane (simpler) when the data types and tools don't matter. Prefer process when each step's input/output payload and responsible team must be legible at a glance.
22: 
23: This type is **parametric** — the inputs schema in §2 drives every coordinate via the formulas in §3. Two generations from the same inputs must produce visually identical SVG. The rule shapes mirror `type-data-flow.md` so color override, IN/OUT chip semantic, and reproducibility checklist read identically across types.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. INPUTS — THE PARAMETER CONTRACT
28: 
29: ```yaml
30: lanes:                              # 1..6 horizontal swimlanes (top to bottom)
31:   - { name: ["RD&E"],                 key: "RDE" }
32:   - { name: ["IT"],                   key: "IT"  }
33:   - { name: ["FIELD", "SERVICES"],    key: "FLD" }
34:   - { name: ["SURVEY", "SERVICES"],   key: "SVY" }
35:   - { name: ["HOUSEHOLD", "UNIT"],    key: "HHU" }
36:   - { name: ["COMMS &", "MARKETING"], key: "CMM" }
37: 
38: steps:                              # 1..12 vertical step columns (left to right)
39:   - { number: "1",  label: "Design"   }
40:   - { number: "2",  label: "Build"    }
41:   - { number: "3",  label: "Test", focal: true }       # focal step header chip — accent fill
42:   - { number: "4",  label: "Train"    }
43:   # ... up to 12
44: 
45: nodes:                              # explicit per-cell entries; empty cells render nothing
46:   - { lane: "RDE", step: 0,  title: "Survey design",      sub: "questionnaire · sampling", tool: "Excel · CSPro",
47:       chips: {in: null,  out: "FL"} }              # first step has no input chip
48:   - { lane: "IT",  step: 1,  title: "Build app",          sub: "form + validation",        tool: "CSPro · scripts",
49:       chips: {in: "FL", out: "TB"}, color: "#5a7d9a" }    # slate-blue — data quality concern
50:   - { lane: "RDE", step: 2,  title: "Pilot test",         sub: "field debug",              tool: "tablet · script",
51:       chips: {in: "TB", out: "TB"}, focal: true }   # focal node — accent border
52:   - { lane: "FLD", step: 3,  title: "Train enumerators",  sub: "protocols · safety",       tool: "manual",
53:       chips: {in: "TB", out: "LS"}, color: "#b85450" }    # rust-red — governance / training
54:   # ... etc
55: 
56: arrows:                             # explicit edges; styles bind to topology (see §4)
57:   - { from: {lane: "RDE", step: 0}, to: {lane: "IT",  step: 1}, style: "normal" }
58:   - { from: {lane: "IT",  step: 1}, to: {lane: "RDE", step: 2}, style: "focal-in" }     # accent — into focal
59:   - { from: {lane: "RDE", step: 2}, to: {lane: "FLD", step: 3}, style: "focal-out" }    # accent — out of focal
60:   - { from: {lane: "RDE", step: 2}, to: {lane: "IT",  step: 1}, style: "trigger" }      # dashed trigger
61:   # ... etc
62: 
63: dark: false
64: ```
65: 
66: **Reserved field semantics:**
67: - `lanes[k].key` — the 3-letter role badge text shown inside every node in that lane.
68: - `lanes[k].name` — 1 or 2 line lane label; uppercase mono.
69: - `steps[j].focal: true` — exactly **one** step may declare this. Header chip renders in accent.
70: - `nodes[i].focal: true` — exactly **one** node may declare this. Renders with accent border (§6).
71: - `nodes[i].chips` — `{in: "<CODE>", out: "<CODE>"}` object (either side `null` to omit). Codes from §9. **Skip** the input chip on the first step's nodes, **skip** the output chip on the last step's nodes (no upstream / downstream).
72: - `nodes[i].color` — optional **per-node color override**. Any valid `"#hex"` string; the §5 palette is recommended for cross-diagram consistency.
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 3. LAYOUT FORMULAS — DETERMINISTIC GEOMETRY
77: 
78: ```
79: label_col_w      = 140
80: step_slot_w      = 112                                # 100-px node + 12-px corridor
81: right_pad        = 28
82: n_steps          = len(steps)
83: n_lanes          = len(lanes)
84: 
85: # Canvas
86: viewBox_w        = label_col_w + n_steps * step_slot_w + right_pad   # 11 steps → 1400
87: header_h         = 36
88: lane_h           = 80
89: has_color_row    = any(node.color or step.color or lane.color in inputs)
90: legend_h         = 100 if has_color_row else 80       # 4 rows when colors are present
91: viewBox_h        = header_h + n_lanes * lane_h + legend_h            # 6 lanes, no colors → 596; with → 616
92: 
93: # Header strip (top)
94: chip_y           = 8
95: chip_w           = 16                                  # 20 if step.number has 2 digits
96: chip_h           = 16
97: chip_rx          = 8                                   # pill
98: 
99: # Lane positions
100: lane_y_top(k)    = header_h + k * lane_h               # 36, 116, 196, 276, 356, 436
101: lane_y_mid(k)    = lane_y_top(k) + lane_h/2            # 76, 156, 236, 316, 396, 476
102: lane_label_x     = label_col_w / 2                     # 70
103: 
104: # Step / node centers
105: step_cx(j)       = label_col_w + 8 + j * step_slot_w + node_w/2      # 198, 310, 422, ...
106:                                                                       # (8-px gutter inside content area)
107: 
108: # Nodes
109: node_w           = 100
110: node_h           = 64
111: node_x(j)        = step_cx(j) - node_w/2
112: node_y(k)        = lane_y_top(k) + (lane_h - node_h)/2     # 8-px top/bottom margin inside lane
113: 
114: # Legend strip (bottom)
115: legend_y_top     = header_h + n_lanes * lane_h
116: legend_row_y     = [legend_y_top + 16, legend_y_top + 37,
117:                     legend_y_top + 58, legend_y_top + 79]
118: ```
119: 
120: ### 3.1 Background structure
121: 
122: - Paper fill across full viewBox.
123: - Dot pattern: 22×22 grid, `circle r=0.8`, `fill rgba(45,49,66,0.10)`. Opacity 0.55.
124: - Alternating lane tints: odd-indexed lanes (0, 2, …) receive `rgba(45,49,66,0.018)` fill from `x=140` to `viewBox_w`.
125: - Lane dividers: horizontal hairlines at every `lane_y_top(k)` and at `legend_y_top`; stroke `rgba(45,49,66,0.12)` width 0.8.
126: - Label column right border: vertical hairline at `x = label_col_w`, stroke `rgba(45,49,66,0.20)` width 1, from `y = header_h` to `y = legend_y_top`.
127: 
128: ### 3.2 Step header chip + label
129: 
130: Per step `j`:
131: 
132: ```
133: chip_w(j)        = 20 if len(step.number) >= 2 else 16
134: chip_x(j)        = step_cx(j) - chip_w(j)/2
135: number_anchor    = (step_cx(j), chip_y + 11)
136: label_anchor     = (step_cx(j), 32)              # 8-px gap below chip
137: ```
138: 
139: **Chip** (the numbered pill at the top of each column):
140: - Default fill: `rgba(45,49,66,0.12)`, number text ink.
141: - Focal fill: `rgba(235,108,54,0.20)`, number text accent (§6).
142: - Per-step `color` override (§5): replaces the fill with `rgba(C, 0.20)` and the number fill with `C`.
143: 
144: **Label** (the uppercase mono text below the chip):
145: - Renders `steps[j].label` (uppercased), anchored at `label_anchor`.
146: - Font: Geist Mono 6 px, weight 500, `letter-spacing="0.12em"`, `text-anchor="middle"`.
147: - Default fill: muted (`#4f5d75` light / `#bfc0c0` dark).
148: - Focal fill: accent (`#eb6c36` light / `#f08a59` dark).
149: - Per-step `color` override: fill = `C` (matches the chip number color).
150: - Keep labels short (≤ 9 chars). Long labels truncate; if you need more, abbreviate.
151: 
152: ### 3.3 Lane labels
153: 
154: One or two-line mono label, all uppercase, letter-spacing 0.08em, font-size 8, fill muted. Centered at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k))`:
155: - Single-line: anchored at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) + 4)`
156: - Two-line: lines at `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) - 4)` and `(lane_label_x, lane_y_mid(k) + 4)`
157: 
158: Per-lane `color` override (§5): replaces the label fill with `C` and the lane stripe tint with `rgba(C, 0.04)`.
159: 
160: ### 3.4 Node content layout (inside the 100×64 rect)
161: 
162: ```
163: role_chip          rect 14×10 at (node_x+4, node_y+4),  rx=2
164: role_chip_text     centered at (node_x+11, node_y+12), font-size=6, weight=600
165:                                                                 # text = lanes[k].key (3-letter lane code)
166: title              centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+26),  font-size=9 sans semibold
167: in→out             centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+40),  font-size=6.5 mono muted
168: tool               centered at (step_cx(j), node_y+52),  font-size=6.5 mono soft
169: data chip IN       rect 16×8 at (node_x+4,   node_y+54), rx=2      # payload entering
170: data chip OUT      rect 16×8 at (node_x+80,  node_y+54), rx=2      # payload leaving
171: ```
172: 
173: **Role chip text rule:** the badge inside each node renders `lanes[k].key` where `k` is the node's lane index — **not** the step number (the step number already lives in the column header chip at the top, §3.2). Showing the lane key as the node badge gives each node a self-contained "who" identifier that survives when a single node is excerpted out of context. Mirrors the same rule in `type-data-flow.md` §3.4.
174: 
175: Empty cells (no node entry) render **nothing**. No placeholder rect, no role chip, no label.
176: 
177: **Chip-vs-tool-text collision rule:** chips sit at `node_y + 54..62`; tool text baseline is at `node_y + 52`. If a node has a two-line title (rare), increase node_h to 72 OR omit the chips for that node. Default behaviour: omit chips on collision.

181: ## 4. CONNECTOR RULES (MANDATORY)
182: 
183: Three styles, bound to topology. Connectors drawn **before** all node rects (z-order rule).
184: 
185: | `style` | Stroke | Width | Dash | Marker | When required |
186: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
187: | `normal` | `#4f5d75` (muted) | 1.0 | — | `arrow` | Standard data hand-off between steps or actors. Unlabelled. |
188: | `focal-in` / `focal-out` | `#eb6c36` (accent) | 1.2 | — | `arrow-accent` | Every edge whose endpoint is the focal node (`focal-in`) or origin is the focal node (`focal-out`). |
189: | `trigger` | `#4f5d75` (muted) | 1.0 | `4,3` | `arrow-sm` | Orchestration trigger (scheduler → tool, manual override → upstream step). Unlabelled. |
190: 
191: **Defs block** (required, three markers):
192: 
193: ```svg
194: <defs>
195:   <pattern id="dots" width="22" height="22" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
196:     <circle cx="11" cy="11" r="0.8" fill="rgba(45,49,66,0.10)"/>
197:   </pattern>
198:   <marker id="arrow"        markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="#4f5d75"/></marker>
199:   <marker id="arrow-accent" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="#eb6c36"/></marker>
200:   <marker id="arrow-sm"     markerWidth="6" markerHeight="5" refX="5" refY="2.5" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 6 2.5, 0 5" fill="#4f5d75"/></marker>
201: </defs>
202: ```
203: 
204: ### 4.1 Routing rules (non-negotiable)
205: 
206: **Single-bend right-angle:** exit RIGHT → corridor → enter TOP (↓ destination below) or BOTTOM (↑ destination above).
207: 
208: - Source-side: exit at `(node_x + 100, lane_y_mid(src_lane))` — node's right edge, vertical center.
209: - Destination-side: enter at `(step_cx(dst_step), node_y(dst_lane))` for downward, or `(step_cx(dst_step), node_y(dst_lane) + 64)` for upward.
210: - Corner radius: 8-px Q-bezier at the bend.
211: - Same-lane edges (rare — same lane, adjacent steps): horizontal `<line>` from src right to dst left.
212: - **No diagonals.** **No left-side entry.** **No exit from the top/bottom of a node.**
213: 
214: ```svg
215: <!-- Downward (destination lane > source lane) -->
216: <path d="M {rx},{src_cy} H {dst_cx - 8} Q {dst_cx},{src_cy} {dst_cx},{src_cy + 8} V {dst_top}"
217:       fill="none" stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
218: 
219: <!-- Upward (destination lane < source lane) -->
220: <path d="M {rx},{src_cy} H {dst_cx - 8} Q {dst_cx},{src_cy} {dst_cx},{src_cy - 8} V {dst_bottom}"
221:       fill="none" stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
222: 
223: <!-- Same lane (adjacent step) -->
224: <line x1="{src_right}" y1="{lane_cy}" x2="{dst_left}" y2="{lane_cy}"
225:       stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
226: ```
227: 
228: - **Z-order:** all `<path>` and `<line>` connectors emitted **before** any node `<rect>`.
229: - **Markers:** exactly one `marker-end` per path. Never `marker-start`.
230: - **Labels:** all process arrows are unlabelled by default. The step number + the actor lane carry the semantic; a label on every arrow is noise. Only label an arrow if it represents a non-step concept (re-test loop, escalation) — then use a paper-masked rect behind 6.5-px mono text.
231: 
232: ### 4.2 Crossings
233: 
234: Avoid. The corridor x position (8 px before destination node) is the only routing column — if two arrows would cross there, **swap step assignments** or **split into two diagrams** rather than introducing a bend-around. Crossings hide the underlying control flow.
235:

238: ## 5. COMPONENT COLOR OVERRIDE
239: 
240: Any node, lane, or step accepts an optional `color: "#hex"`. Mirrors `type-data-flow.md` §5 and `type-high-level.md` §4.4 so the rule reads identically across types.
241: 
242: ### 5.1 Per-node `color`
243: 
244: Applied to:
245: 
246: | Element | Light | Dark |
247: |---|---|---|
248: | Container fill (`rect`) | `rgba(C, 0.06)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.10)` |
249: | Container stroke | `rgba(C, 0.35)` (stroke-width 1) | `rgba(C_light, 0.45)` |
250: | Role chip fill | `rgba(C, 0.18)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.22)` |
251: | Role chip text | `C` | `C_light` |
252: | Title text | `C` | `C_light` |
253: | Sub-label (in → out) | **unchanged** (muted) | **unchanged** (muted) |
254: | Tool label | **unchanged** (soft) | **unchanged** (soft) |
255: | Data-type chips | **unchanged** | **unchanged** |
256: | Arrows touching this node | **unchanged** — topology-driven | **unchanged** |
257: 
258: `C_light` = the same hex lightened ~15% for dark-mode contrast (e.g., `#b85450` → `#d97a78`).
259: 
260: ### 5.2 Per-step `color`
261: 
262: Replaces the step header chip's fill with `rgba(C, 0.20)` and the chip's number text fill with `C`. The legend's matching step entry uses the same colors.
263: 
264: ### 5.3 Per-lane `color`
265: 
266: Replaces the lane stripe tint with `rgba(C, 0.04)` and the lane label text fill with `C`. Use sparingly — lane tints are easy to over-apply.
267: 
268: ### 5.4 Rules
269: 
270: - **Never on focal nodes / focal steps.** The accent already carries that signal. A `color` on a focal element is ignored.
271: - **Never on arrows.** Arrows are topology-driven. If you want a colored edge, pick a different `style` from §4, not a color override.
272: - **Cap at 3 custom-colored elements** per diagram (nodes + lanes + steps combined), in addition to the focal pair (focal node + focal step header). Above 3 the visual signal starts to fragment.
273: - **Subtitle and tool labels stay muted** regardless of any component `color`.
274: 
275: ### 5.5 Semantic palette (recommended)
276: 
277: Same palette as `type-high-level.md`, `type-dp-integration.md`, `type-data-flow.md`:
278: 
279: - `#b85450` rust-red — Security / Identity / Governance (access control, training, approvals)
280: - `#5a7d9a` slate-blue — Observability / Quality (data quality gates, validation, monitoring)
281: - `#7a8c47` olive-green — Data Products / Publication (consumer-ready outputs, releases)
282: - `#8c6d3f` warm-brown — Backup / DR / Archive

286: ## 6. FOCAL RULE
287: 
288: The process diagram has three focal slots, exactly one entry each:
289: 
290: - **One focal step** (`steps[j].focal: true`) — typically the analytical or decision pivot (Test, Approve, Validate). Header chip and legend chip render in accent.
291: - **One focal node** (`nodes[i].focal: true`) — the node that *receives* the critical handoff. Accent border + accent role chip + ink title (title text stays ink so it's still readable; only the border + role chip carry the accent).
292: - **One focal arrow set** (`style: focal-in` and `focal-out`) — edges into and out of the focal node. Accent solid strokes.
293: 
294: If zero or >1 of any focal slot are declared, halt and ask the user.

321: ## 8. REPRODUCIBILITY CHECKLIST (TASTE GATE)
322: 
323: Before emitting SVG, verify **every** item:
324: 
325: 1. `viewBox = "0 0 {viewBox_w} {viewBox_h}"` derived via §3.
326: 2. Header strip at `y=0..36`; legend strip at `y=legend_y_top..viewBox_h` (`legend_y_top = 36 + n_lanes * 80`).
327: 3. Every node at `(step_cx(j) - 50, lane_y_top(k) + 8)` size `100×64`.
328: 4. Empty cells render nothing — no placeholder rect, no text.
329: 5. Exactly **one** focal step (`steps[j].focal: true`).
330: 6. Exactly **one** focal node (`nodes[i].focal: true`).
331: 7. Focal-touching arrows use `style: focal-in` / `focal-out` (accent).
332: 8. All other arrows `style: normal` (muted solid) or `style: trigger` (muted dashed). Unlabelled by default.
333: 9. All arrows emitted before any node rect (z-order rule).
334: 10. Single-bend right-angle routing only — exit right, enter top/bottom. No diagonals. Q-bezier `r=8` at each bend.
335: 11. Custom component colors ≤ 3 (in addition to the focal pair). Arrows never recolored by component `color`.
336: 12. Subtitle and tool labels stay muted regardless of any component `color`. Input chip skipped on first step's nodes, output chip skipped on last step's nodes.

340: ## 9. DATA-TYPE CHIPS REFERENCE (INPUT + OUTPUT)
341: 
342: Same catalog as `type-data-flow.md` §9.
343: 
344: - **Input chip** at `(node_x+4, node_y+54)` — bottom-**left**. Payload entering the node.
345: - **Output chip** at `(node_x+80, node_y+54)` — bottom-**right**. Payload leaving the node.
346: - Either chip may be omitted (first/last step, unknown payload).
347: 
348: ### Chip codes
349: 
350: | Code | Color (light) | Color (dark) | Meaning |
351: |------|---------------|--------------|---------|
352: | `LS` | `#7c8f6f` sage | `#9caf8f` | List / assignment / task |
353: | `DB` | `#5c7899` dusty-blue | `#82a0c0` | Dataset / tabular records |
354: | `TB` | `#b8915a` mustard | `#d3ad7a` | Table (analysis-ready) |
355: | `FL` | `#9c6b50` rust-brown | `#b88670` | File / document / report |
356: | `WB` | `#6e6479` slate | `#8d8298` | Web / press / public release |
357: | N/A | omit chip entirely | — | Unknown or not applicable |
358: 
359: Text inside chip: white, font-size 5, weight 700, mono.
360: 
361: Data-type chip colors are a **separate semantic axis** from the per-node color override (§5). Chip colors describe *payload format*; node color describes *concern type*. A node can have both an `out: TB` mustard chip and a rust-red border simultaneously.

365: ## 10. LEGEND (3- OR 4-ROW STRIP)
366: 
367: Each row introduced by a category label at `x = label_col_w + 4` (= 144). The default legend has **3 rows** (`STEPS` / `DATA TYPE` / `FLOW`); when one or more nodes carry a `color` override (§5), add a 4th `CONCERN` row and grow `legend_h` to 100.
368: 
369: - **Row 1 — `STEPS`** at `y = legend_y_top + 16`: repeat the header chips with their labels. Focal step keeps accent fill.
370: - **Row 2 — `DATA TYPE`** at `y = legend_y_top + 37`: one swatch per chip type actually used in the diagram. Append a small sub-hint in muted mono: `left chip = input · right chip = output`.
371: - **Row 3 — `CONCERN`** (only when color overrides are present) at `y = legend_y_top + 58`: one mini-rect per custom color used, with its semantic label.
372: - **Row 4 — `FLOW`** (position depends on whether `CONCERN` row exists): one segment per arrow style actually used, with marker + label.

378: | Dimension | Max |
379: |---|---|
380: | Lanes (actors) | 6 |
381: | Steps | 12 |
382: | Nodes per lane | Nodes = active steps only — empty cells are invisible |
383: | Labelled arrows | 0 by default (label only for non-step concepts) |
384: | Data-type chips per node | 2 (input + output) |
385: | Custom-colored elements (§5) | 3 (in addition to focal node + focal step) |

391: ## 12. ANTI-PATTERNS
392: 
393: - **Placeholder empty cells** — if an actor doesn't participate in a step, leave the cell empty (no box, no text).
394: - **Diagonal arrows** — every connector must have exactly one right-angle bend. No direct straight lines between nodes in different lanes.
395: - **Left/right port entry on a vertical-dominant arrow** — always exit right, enter top or bottom.
396: - **More than one focal step / focal node** — pick the single most critical operation.
397: - **Unlabelled lanes** — every swimlane must identify its actor.
398: - **All arrows the same style** — orchestration triggers must be dashed to distinguish them from data-flow connectors.
399: - **`color` override on a focal element** — ignored. Accent always wins.
400: - **Custom-colored arrows** — connectors are topology-driven; `color` on a node never spreads to its edges.
401: - **Lane tints over-applied** — a tint on every lane reads as decoration, not signal. Apply to ≤1 lane.
402: - **Data-type chips in a double-line-name node** — skip the chips or shorten the name to one line.
403: - **More than 12 steps without splitting** — use an overview + detail pair.

18:

42: - Optional left-margin axis arrow + Geist Mono label (`rarer ↑`, `drop-off ↓`).

45:

15: # Scatter Plot
16: 
17: ## 1. OVERVIEW
18: 
19: **Best for:** correlation and distribution — two continuous variables plotted against each other. Use when the relationship (or lack of one) between variables is the message, or when you need to identify clusters, outliers, and high/low performers.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
24: 
25: - **Plot area margins:** left 80px, bottom 60px, top 40px, right 40px — inside `0 0 1000 500` viewBox.
26: - **Point count:** 5–30 points. Fewer → just describe the relationship in prose; more → bin into a density contour.
27: - **Axes:** X at y=420 (baseline), Y at x=80. Both use Geist Mono 8px gridline labels. Gridlines 4–6 per axis at equal intervals.
28: - **Point shape:** `<circle>` r=5 for standard points, r=6 for focal. Focal point in `accent` fill. Others in `muted @ 0.20` fill + `muted` stroke.
29: - **Labels on points (optional):** Geist Mono 8px next to a point. Use a paper-fill rect mask behind the label. Label at most 2–3 points; not all.
30: - **Trend line (optional):** `<line>` from lower-left to upper-right, stroke `rgba(45,49,66,0.25)` dashed 4,3. Never force a perfect fit — only add if the trend is visually obvious.
31: - **Quadrant dividers (optional):** light dashed lines at the median x and y to split into quadrants. Label each quadrant in Geist Mono 8px, muted.
32: 
33: ### Point pattern
34: 
35: ```svg
36: <!-- Non-focal point — paper mask + circle -->
37: <circle cx="X" cy="Y" r="5" fill="#f5f5f5"/>
38: <circle cx="X" cy="Y" r="5" fill="rgba(79,93,117,0.20)" stroke="#4f5d75" stroke-width="1"/>
39: 
40: <!-- Focal point -->
41: <circle cx="X" cy="Y" r="6" fill="#f5f5f5"/>
42: <circle cx="X" cy="Y" r="6" fill="rgba(235,108,54,0.15)" stroke="#eb6c36" stroke-width="1.2"/>
43: ```
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ## 3. ANTI-PATTERNS
48: 
49: - More than 30 points without clustering (jitter/mush).
50: - Forced trend line when the data is genuinely scattered — dishonest.
51: - Point labels on every point (label the focal and 1–2 notable outliers only).
52: - Bubble size encoding (use a third axis label or color instead; bubble area perception is unreliable).
53: - Axes that don't include zero when the absolute position matters; axes that do include zero when the range is tiny and far from zero.
54: 
55: ---
56:

59: - `assets/diagrams/scatter.html` — minimal light
60: - `assets/diagrams/scatter-dark.html` — minimal dark
61: - `assets/diagrams/scatter-full.html` — full editorial

19: **Best for:** correlation and distribution — two continuous variables plotted against each other. Use when the relationship (or lack of one) between variables is the message, or when you need to identify clusters, outliers, and high/low performers.
20: 
21: ---
22:

24: 
25: - **Plot area margins:** left 80px, bottom 60px, top 40px, right 40px — inside `0 0 1000 500` viewBox.
26: - **Point count:** 5–30 points. Fewer → just describe the relationship in prose; more → bin into a density contour.
27: - **Axes:** X at y=420 (baseline), Y at x=80. Both use Geist Mono 8px gridline labels. Gridlines 4–6 per axis at equal intervals.
28: - **Point shape:** `<circle>` r=5 for standard points, r=6 for focal. Focal point in `accent` fill. Others in `muted @ 0.20` fill + `muted` stroke.
29: - **Labels on points (optional):** Geist Mono 8px next to a point. Use a paper-fill rect mask behind the label. Label at most 2–3 points; not all.
30: - **Trend line (optional):** `<line>` from lower-left to upper-right, stroke `rgba(45,49,66,0.25)` dashed 4,3. Never force a perfect fit — only add if the trend is visually obvious.
31: - **Quadrant dividers (optional):** light dashed lines at the median x and y to split into quadrants. Label each quadrant in Geist Mono 8px, muted.
32: 
33: ### Point pattern
34: 
35: ```svg
36: <!-- Non-focal point — paper mask + circle -->
37: <circle cx="X" cy="Y" r="5" fill="#f5f5f5"/>
38: <circle cx="X" cy="Y" r="5" fill="rgba(79,93,117,0.20)" stroke="#4f5d75" stroke-width="1"/>
39: 
40: <!-- Focal point -->
41: <circle cx="X" cy="Y" r="6" fill="#f5f5f5"/>
42: <circle cx="X" cy="Y" r="6" fill="rgba(235,108,54,0.15)" stroke="#eb6c36" stroke-width="1.2"/>
43: ```

46: 
47: ## 3. ANTI-PATTERNS
48: 
49: - More than 30 points without clustering (jitter/mush).
50: - Forced trend line when the data is genuinely scattered — dishonest.
51: - Point labels on every point (label the focal and 1–2 notable outliers only).
52: - Bubble size encoding (use a third axis label or color instead; bubble area perception is unreliable).
53: - Axes that don't include zero when the absolute position matters; axes that do include zero when the range is tiny and far from zero.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 4. EXAMPLES
58: 
59: - `assets/diagrams/scatter.html` — minimal light
60: - `assets/diagrams/scatter-dark.html` — minimal dark
61: - `assets/diagrams/scatter-full.html` — full editorial

18: 
19: **Best for:** comparing 3–5 entities across 3–5 quantitative criteria on a single normalized 0–N scale. Capability matrices, product or backend evaluations, framework/team scorecards. 20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
24: 
25: - **N axes (3–5).** Equally spaced on a regular polygon-N. First axis at the top (`-90°`), going clockwise. **Above 5 → split or use a comparison table.**

27: - **Axis spokes** from center to each outer vertex. `rule-solid` 0.20 opacity. **No arrowheads.**
28: - **Axis labels:** one word per spoke (Jobs-minimal). Geist sans 11px weight 600. Place 16px outside the outer ring along the axis vector. Top/bottom = `text-anchor="middle"`; right side = `start`; left side = `end`.
29: - **Scale ticks** (e.g. `2 4 6 8 10`) only on the **first (top) axis** — putting numbers on every spoke clutters the chart fast. Geist Mono 8px, `muted`, anchored end at `cx − 6`.
30: - **Series polygon:** stroke 1.5px at the series color, fill the same color at `0.18` opacity (`0.22` in dark). Stroke 1.8px on the focal series — a subtle weight bump.
31: - **Vertex dots:** **only on the focal series**, `r=4` filled with the series color. Non-focal series are stroke-and-fill only. This is the load-bearing rule that keeps the chart readable at 4–5 series.
32: - **Drawing order:** dots-pattern bg → grid rings → axis spokes → axis labels → scale ticks → non-focal series (smallest area first) → focal series → focal vertex dots → legend.
33: - **Legend:** horizontal strip at the bottom (per the global rule). Swatch is a 16×8 rectangle (matches the polygon stroke+fill, not a circle), then the entity name. ~140px between entries. Optional italic tail on the right with the rationale (`"One coral. Position is the signal — color reserved for the recommended option."`).
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## 3. MATH
38: 
39: For axis `i` (0-indexed) of `N`, value `v` on scale `S`, center `(cx, cy)`, outer radius `R`:
40: 
41: ```
42: angle = -π/2 + 2π · i / N
43: x = cx + (v / S) · R · cos(angle)
44: y = cy + (v / S) · R · sin(angle)
45: ```
46: 
47: A series with values `[v0, v1, ..., v(N-1)]` becomes a `<polygon>` with `points="x0,y0 x1,y1 ..."`.
48: 
49: ### Pre-computed reference (N=5, cx=500, cy=240, R=160, S=10, integer-rounded)
50: 
51: | Fraction `f` | i=0 (top) | i=1 | i=2 | i=3 | i=4 |
52: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
53: | 0.2 | 500,208 | 530,230 | 519,266 | 481,266 | 470,230 |
54: | 0.4 | 500,176 | 561,220 | 538,292 | 462,292 | 439,220 |
55: | 0.6 | 500,144 | 591,211 | 556,317 | 444,317 | 409,211 |
56: | 0.8 | 500,112 | 622,201 | 575,343 | 425,343 | 378,201 |
57: | 1.0 | 500,80  | 652,191 | 594,369 | 406,369 | 348,191 |
58: 
59: For an arbitrary value `v` on axis `i`, take the unit offset from the row above for that axis (e.g. axis 1: offset `(152, -49)` from center) and scale by `v/S`. **Drop coords as integers — fractional pixels in SVG render fine, but integers keep the file scannable.**
60: 
61: ### Worked example (N=5)
62: 
63: Series `[9, 8, 9, 9, 9]` on a 0–10 scale becomes:
64: 
65: ```svg

67:          fill="rgba(235,108,54,0.18)" stroke="#eb6c36" stroke-width="1.8"/>
68: ```
69: 
70: Each vertex: `center + (v/10) · (outer_i − center)`, rounded to the nearest pixel.
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## 4. SERIES PALETTE
75: 
76: The skill's "1-focal" rule still holds: `accent` is reserved for the focal series, and a small editorial palette (`series-1` through `series-5`, defined in [`style-guide.md`](../foundations/style-guide.md)) covers the non-focal series. Don't reach for free-form colors.
77: 
78: | Slot | Token | Light | Dark |
79: |---|---|---|---|
80: | Focal | `accent` | `#eb6c36` | `#f08a59` |
81: | 1 | `series-1` (sage) | `#7c8f6f` | `#9caf8f` |
82: | 2 | `series-2` (dusty-blue) | `#5c7899` | `#82a0c0` |
83: | 3 | `series-3` (mustard) | `#b8915a` | `#d3ad7a` |
84: | 4 | `series-4` (rust-brown) | `#9c6b50` | `#b88670` |
85: | 5 | `series-5` (slate) | `#6e6479` | `#8d8298` |
86:

88: 
89: ## 5. ANTI-PATTERNS
90: 
91: - **More than 5 series** → mush. Split into two charts (e.g. "best by latency" + "best by ops") or switch to a comparison table.
92: - **Axes on inconsistent native scales** (one 0–100, another 0–1) without normalization. **Always normalize to 0–N first** — radar polygons compare *shapes*, not absolute values.

95: - **Radar with 2 series** — a comparison bar chart or a 2-row table is clearer.

98: - **Rainbow palette.** Even with the new `series-*` tokens, you don't need all 5 in one chart — use only as many as you have non-focal entities.
99: 
100: ---

105: - `assets/diagrams/radar-dark.html` — minimal dark, same data.
106: - `assets/diagrams/radar-full.html` — full editorial: container framing + 4 cards (one per backend) with varied widths + footer.

16: # Data Flow
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: **Best for:** visualising how data moves through a pipeline *across organisational roles* — who initiates, who processes, who publishes, and who consumes. The canonical use case is a multi-role data platform (Admin → Engineers → Scientists → Consumers) with 4–6 process steps. Use when the reader needs to understand **who does what at each stage**, not just the technical components.
21: 
22: Prefer standard **Swimlane** for cross-functional business processes (HR approvals, support tickets). Use **Data flow** when the subject is a data pipeline with typed payloads (raw files, tables, reports) and role-scoped access boundaries.
23:

# Architecture

## 1. OVERVIEW

**Best for:** system overviews, data-flow diagrams, integration maps, infra topology.

---

## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
- Group components by tier or trust boundary (frontend → backend → data; public → private).

- Draw arrows before boxes so z-order puts connections behind components.

===== type-bar
contextType: implementation
version: 1.2.1.0
---

# Bar / Column Chart

## 1. OVERVIEW

**Best for:** comparing discrete quantities across categories or time intervals — sprint velocity, monthly revenue, feature adoption, cohort counts. Use when each category has a single numeric value and the comparison between bars is the primary message.

---

## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS

- **Orientation:** Vertical bars (columns) are default. Horizontal bars are appropriate when category labels are long or you have more than 8 categories.
- **Plot area margins:** left 80px (y-axis labels), bottom 60px (x-axis labels), top 40px, right 40px — inside a `0 0 1000 500` viewBox.
- **Bar count cap:** 4–8 bars. More than 8 → group into periods or split into two charts.
- **Bar width:** ≥ 50% of the column pitch (the gap should never exceed the bar). Typical: pitch=110px, bar=72px.
- **Y-axis gridlines:** 4–6 horizontal lines at regular intervals. Stroke `rgba(45,49,66,0.08)` (very faint), 0.8px. X-axis baseline at `rgba(45,49,66,0.25)`, 1px.
===== type-sequence
version: 1.2.1.0
---

# Sequence

## 1. OVERVIEW

**Best for:** request/response flows, protocol exchanges, multi-actor interactions over time, API call traces, incident reconstructions, auth/token refresh paths with branching.

---

## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
- Actors as boxes in a horizontal row at the top.
- **Lifelines**: dashed vertical lines descending from each actor to the bottom.
- Messages: horizontal arrows between lifelines; time flows top→down.
- **Activation bar**: narrow rectangle (`w=8`, muted fill, 0.8 hairline stroke) on a lifeline spanning the interval that actor holds control. Stack for nested calls.
- Self-messages: short U-shaped loop returning to the same lifeline; label right of the loop.
- Return messages: **dashed** stroke + **filled** marker (never open). Prefer muted; optionally match the originating call color when pairing multi-hop stacks. Headline success may use solid coral (see Message kinds).
- Coral on the primary success response or headline message — one, maybe two. Actor focal strokes do not count toward the coral message budget.
===== type-loop
version: 1.2.2.0
---

# Loop

## 1. OVERVIEW

**Best for:** reinforcing cycles, flywheels, feedback loops, and operating loops — anything where the last step feeds the first and a shared hub accumulates state. Use Loop when the reader must see both motions at once: work advances clockwise around the ring, while each pass writes durable state back to one common center.

Prefer **Flowchart** when the path ends, branches toward an outcome, or never truly returns to its first step. Prefer **Cycle** when the center does not accumulate shared state. The dashed write-back spokes are the defining signal here: remove them and the figure is only a circular process.

This type is **parametric**. The inputs in §2 determine station count, angles, edge intersections, connector paths, and viewBox bounds. Identical inputs should produce identical geometry.

---

## 2. INPUTS — THE PARAMETER CONTRACT

```yaml
title: "The self-improving loop"
===== type-layers
version: 1.2.1.0
---

# Layer Stack

## 1. OVERVIEW

**Best for:** OSI model, CSS cascade, context hierarchy, tech stack, abstraction layers, memory hierarchy.

---

## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
- Horizontal bands stacked vertically. Each layer is a full-width rectangle (same x, same width). 4–6 layers total.
- Layer height 56–72px, width typically 800–880px inside a 1000px viewBox.
- Each row contains (left→right):
  1. **Index tag** on the far left (`L3`, `07`, `APPLICATION`) — Geist Mono 8–9px eyebrow.
  2. **Layer name** slightly right of center-left — Geist 14–16px 600.
  3. **Sublabel / note** on the far right — Geist Mono 9–10px muted.
- Border between layers: 1px hairline `rgba(45,49,66,0.12)`. Outer silhouette 1px ink or muted.
===== type-venn
version: 1.2.1.0
---

# Venn / Set Overlap

## 1. OVERVIEW

**Best for:** intersection of concepts/domains, shared attributes between categories, "where A meets B", ikigai-style frames (desirable × feasible × viable).

---

## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
- **Prefer 2 or 3 circles.** Avoid 4+ (unreadable — use a matrix instead).
- Circle stroke: 1px hairline, color per-set (ink, muted, soft).
- Circle fill: very low-opacity tint — `rgba(45,49,66,0.04)` for ink set, `rgba(79,93,117,0.05)` for muted. Tints compound naturally in overlap regions.
- Radii: equal when sets are comparable in size; proportional when sets are meaningfully different. Don't fake equal sizes for aesthetics.
- **Set labels** placed outside the circle, NEVER crossing the stroke. Geist 12–14px 600 for the set name, optional Geist Mono 9px sublabel.
- **Intersection labels** placed inside the overlap region, Geist 12px 600, centered. For small overlaps, use a leader line to a label in clear space.
- **Coral accent** on the ONE focal intersection — the "sweet spot". Either coral label stroke OR clipPath-bounded coral fill tint (`rgba(235,108,54,0.10)`).
===== type-tree
version: 1.2.1.0
---

# Tree / Hierarchy

## 1. OVERVIEW

**Best for:** org charts, dependency trees, taxonomy, file trees, decision breakdowns, skill trees.

---

## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
- Root at top, children fan out below (or root at left, children to right).
- Nodes are small labeled rectangles (`rx=6`), Geist 12px 600 name + optional Geist Mono 9px sublabel. Width 120–180px, height 40–52px.
- **Connectors are orthogonal (elbow-style), never diagonal.** Parent drops a short vertical line, then a horizontal bus connects siblings, then each child has a short vertical drop into its top edge. 1px muted stroke.
- Leaf indicator: thinner stroke (0.8) or different fill — OR let terminal position do the work.
- Max depth: 4 (root + 3 tiers). Max breadth per level: 5.
- Coral on **one** node: root OR critical leaf. Not both.
- Draw connectors before nodes.

# Review Core Doctrine

Shared doctrine consumed by both `@review` and `@deep-review`.

**Ownership.** This file owns the severity ids and their meanings (section 2), the evidence rules (section 3) and the finding schema (section 7). The deep-review contract, [`review-mode-contract.yaml`](../../../system-deep-loop/deep-review/assets/review-mode-contract.yaml), is an external consumer: it owns the deep-review loop (dimensions, verdicts, severity weights, convergence and quality gates) and reuses the severity ids defined here. - Fix: `cd backend && npm install`. The tool runs its TypeScript directly via `ts-node`; there is no build step.

# Design Token Vocabulary

Shared naming for color, typography, layout, elevation, motion, and state tokens, so a term means the same thing every time a captured surface is recorded as a Style Reference.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

Keep token language consistent when a captured visual system is described, so a name in a Style Reference carries one meaning.

### Usage

Use these terms when naming or grouping the tokens read off an extracted surface. The detailed math behind each token stays with the extraction workflow and the reference format.

---

## 2. COLOR TOKENS

- **Canvas**: the dominant surface color behind content.
- **Surface**: cards, panels, sheets, and contained regions placed on the canvas.
- **Text primary**: the highest-emphasis reading color.
- **Text secondary**: lower-emphasis supporting copy.
- **Accent**: the brand or action color that carries emphasis.
- **Signal**: semantic feedback color such as success, warning, danger, or info.
- **Border**: structural line color for separation without heavy fill.

# Theming a diagram from DESIGN.md

`DESIGN.md` is a style reference, not a diagram form. The diagram packet applies one locally
available v3 reference to a copy of a form: it never fetches a reference, never repaints the stock
forms, and never guesses a colour a reference did not hold.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

Gives a diagram delivery the look of a measured or hand-written brand reference the same way a
chart delivery already gets it, with the diagram's own role vocabulary — structural chrome across
three skins — derived, gated and recorded rather than mapped across from the chart's series model.

### When to Use

- A request names a `DESIGN.md`, a design system, or a look found somewhere that a reference
  generator has turned into a v3 reference file.
- A themed diagram copy is wanted for review while the stock corpus stays untouched.
- The stock look itself is wanted as one reference among several: `--default` is the reference the
  corpus's own palette is written down in.

### Core Principle

A role is filled by what the reference says about it, and when the reference says nothing the role
is either derived mechanically from a role it did say something about, or it keeps the stock value
and the run says so by name. The stock accent's recorded departure is never re-derived into a pass
for a themed value.

24: rather than described, and adjusting one is faster than filling a blank. So the library holds both
25: kinds side by side and neither is precious: 27 canonical diagrams, one per type, 7 variants that
26: demonstrate a specific pattern, and 4 starters for when you want the skin without the drawing.
27: 
28: Nothing here is a strict template. Change the data, the labels, the geometry, the node count. The
29: corpus check holds what a file can be read for: accessibility wiring, the 4px grid, arrow-label mask
30: clearance, unique ids, no external resources, and the palette block on the four starters whose
31: tokens have to match the palette source. It says nothing about what you draw, and it leaves whether
32: connectors meet their targets, overlap, or fan too close together to the judged reads in the capture
33: review.
34: 
35: The four starters are named `starter-light`, `starter-dark`, `starter-terminal` and `starter-full`.
36: They are the only forms that carry a palette block for every role, because they are what a new
37: diagram is copied from; a worked form keeps the tokens it actually draws with. They answer no
38: question of their own, which is why the catalog does not index them.
39: 
40: Inside a starter the drawing references its roles by name rather than by value, so repainting the
41: block repaints the figure. One role is declared without being drawn with: the full starter carries
42: `paper-2` for the framed variant that ships commented out, so uncommenting four lines sits the figure
43: on a card. A role declared for a documented opt-in is the one good reason to declare a role the
44: drawing does not use. Three of the four ship an empty placeholder drawing, so there is nothing
45: in them to repaint until you draw it — that is what makes them starters. The full one carries a
46: worked figure, and theming it moves every mark.
47: 
48: To repaint any of these in another visual language, see
49: [`../../references/design-md-theming.md`](../../references/design-md-theming.md).
